opening: The latch sticks when it gets cold. I said I'd fix it yesterday. I keep saying that.

journal_cue.title: A moved threshold
journal_cue.text: The forest has shifted its doorway. The trail still leads somewhere; the entrance makes no promise about what waits inside.
journal_cue.approach: Let her set the pace. A quiet pause is still part of the conversation.
journal_cue.interpretation: The dream may begin at the house because Mathilda can only approach what feels like home by first moving its door.

journal.title: Rings of wood
journal.text: The cut trees stand at the height of doors. Their pale rings show where each year closed over a wound. The axe has gone, but the wood keeps its shape around the blow.
journal.approach: Stay with the image she chose. You do not have to ask for the whole story.
journal.interpretation: Mathilda turns damage into weather and architecture. It lets her name what happened without naming the person who did it.

interlude: The path has been made to resemble a sentence. I keep waiting for the part where it says who is allowed to leave.
The pale rings look almost like doors drawn from memory. Maybe Mathilda is not showing me how the forest ends, but how she learned to make an exit wherever she could.
beats.text: The trees are cut at doorway height. A tree is a house that learned to stand. The axe thinks strength means permission; the rings remember every blow and call the remembering a season.

journal.title: The late step
journal.text: I stopped. The second set of prints continued for three paces before it noticed. They were already softening at the edges, as if the snow had been asked to forget them.
journal.approach: Offer a choice, then let her decide whether to move, wait, or stop.
journal.interpretation: The late steps could be memory lagging behind the body, or the body waiting to learn whether stopping is safe.

interlude: For a moment the forest is quiet enough to hear the snow choosing which prints to keep.
Three paces after me. Not following, exactly. The dream keeps placing her where a second thought would be: just late enough to feel like mine.
beats.text: The heavier steps are always late. When you stop, they take a moment to notice. Three sisters spin the road: leave, follow, freeze. Old stories call the frozen one faithless. Old stories are told by the living.

journal.title: Witness flame
journal.text: The lantern points into the trees, away from the room it was meant to warm. Its glass is black with soot on one side. Someone has kept the flame alive through the wind.
journal.approach: Ask what would help her feel safer now. Do not make her prove what happened.
journal.interpretation: Perhaps she carries the light outward because looking back at the house costs more than watching the dark.

interlude: I want to turn the lantern around. It isn't mine to point. I can stay long enough to see what it shows.
A light aimed at the trees is still a light left for someone. I cannot tell whether she expects me to follow it or only to know she was here.
beats.text: Someone turned the lantern toward the woods. Prometheus stole a flame and they called it crime. A man takes what is not given and names the silence afterward peace. The lantern knows.

journal.title: Tracks that return
journal.text: Three trails enter the clearing and two come back. At the center, the snow is smooth. No mark says whether the last traveler vanished, waited, or was never there.
journal.approach: Do not treat silence, stillness, or looking back as consent.
journal.interpretation: The missing sister may be Mathilda's name for a self that had to disappear. Or she may be refusing the dream its tidy ending.

interlude: I count the paths twice. The number stays the same; the story changes each time I look away.
Perhaps Mathilda is the missing set of prints. Perhaps she is the one who noticed they were missing. The clearing makes room for both, then calls it snow.
beats.text: Three sets of tracks enter the clearing. Only two return. Orpheus was told not to turn, so the song blames his looking, not the hand that let go.

events.line: Three sisters, all called duty: leave, follow, freeze. They make a maze when someone else chooses the walls.
interlude: Three is an old number for a choice. It is also a useful way to hide that someone else built the choices.
I used to think the hardest part was choosing correctly. Maybe the harder question is who narrowed the road until every direction looked like a test.

journal.title: Three sisters
journal.text: Three sisters, three duties, all waiting for me to call one of them fate. The snow holds each path open without telling me which one a good woman would take.
journal.approach: Offer options without naming one as the brave or correct choice.
journal.interpretation: Mathilda may be testing whether I will mistake survival for a verdict about character.

events.line: Ariadne lays a thread through the dark. The path keeps climbing after the trees end. Sorry. I meant: stay where I can see you.
interlude: She corrects herself before I can answer. The correction feels like a door left on its latch, not quite closed.
Ariadne's thread was supposed to lead out. Mathilda's seems to ask a smaller question: can we remain visible to one another without being tied together?

journal.title: The red thread
journal.text: The red thread leads up toward the tower and vanishes where the branches begin. Ariadne used hers to leave a maze. This one may be there so Mathilda can keep track of who is still in sight.
journal.approach: Follow the detail she offers. Do not pull her toward a confession.
journal.interpretation: The thread might be a way out. Her quick apology suggests it might also be a tether she is afraid to loosen.

events.line: The warm window caught the axe below it. The snow had not covered the handle yet. He had been close. I can tell you more if you want.
interlude: Warmth has gathered behind the glass. I cannot tell if the room is shelter, evidence, or the thing she is trying to approach without entering.
She says the axe was close. My mind supplies a house around it, a witness behind the curtain. It is eager to build a story where the window gives testimony.

journal.title: A warm window
journal.text: A square of gold rests on the snow beneath the window. The axe handle is still dark with meltwater. Someone inside has left a lamp burning, but the curtain does not move.
journal.approach: Ask before coming closer; accept the distance she chooses.
journal.interpretation: The lit room could be a home she misses, or a witness that saw and did not open the door. Mathilda leaves both readings alive.

arrival: The trees are empty. The lantern is still turned toward them.

small_talk.prompt: Sorry. That was a dull way to say hello. Did the cold catch you?
small_talk.guidance: Start with the ordinary. You can keep your distance, wait, or ask her to walk with you.

choices.label: A little cold. I’ll be all right.
choices.background: Cold. Something ordinary to say while I look for the words I came here with.
choices.response: Good. I brought the wrong gloves again. They look warm, which is not the same thing.

journal.title: A little weather
journal.text: You began with the cold. She answered the question you asked, then wandered where she wished.
journal.approach: Small talk can be a safe beginning; let her decide whether to go deeper.

choices.label: I wanted to see you.
choices.background: I wanted to see her. There it is, without the weather around it.
choices.response: Oh. I thought you might. We can stand here for a moment.

journal.title: Wanted to see you
journal.text: You said why you came. She chose to share the moment without closing the distance.
journal.approach: Warmth does not require moving closer. Let her set the distance.

choices.label: Would you walk with me?
choices.background: Two sets of steps. The path might feel different that way.
choices.response: Yes. Slowly, though. The snow is hiding the parts of the path I remember.

journal.title: A slower path
journal.text: You asked to walk together. She agreed, and set the pace.
journal.approach: Offer a choice, then let the other person set the pace.

small_talk.prompt: The path sounds longer from here.
small_talk.guidance: Ask permission before changing distance. Keep the way back open.

choices.label: We don't have to talk about anything.
choices.background: The sentence ends. Nothing rushes in to fill it.
choices.response: The Fates knot the thread when a hand is afraid. I thought the knot meant I had chosen to stay.

journal.title: Permission to pause
journal.text: You let her leave the sentence unfinished.
journal.approach: Do not press for details. Let her decide whether to return to a subject.

choices.label: Would you like me to stand nearer?
choices.background: She is measuring the space between us before I do.
choices.response: That distance is all right. The wolf in the old tale waits outside the ring of fire. Please don't come up behind me.

journal.title: The chosen distance
journal.text: You asked before moving. She named the space that felt all right.
journal.approach: Ask clearly, then respect the first answer. Do not approach from behind.

choices.label: We can go back together.
choices.background: There is a way back. It can stay an offer.
choices.response: I still listen for him when the trees go quiet. The forest has learned his footstep by heart.

journal.title: A way back
journal.text: You offered to leave together. The choice stayed hers.
journal.approach: Offer an exit without taking control of it.

choices.label: Was it the lumberjack? Tell me exactly what he did.
choices.background: I want the name more than I want to hear how this lands.
choices.processing_thought: I want the name more than I want to hear how this lands.
choices.response: The name makes the trees close. I can't give you the whole thing because you asked for it.

journal.title: The question that closes
journal.text: You asked for the whole account before she was ready to give it.
journal.approach: When a question closes the conversation, acknowledge the pressure and return control to her.

small_talk.prompt: I'm sorry. I keep offering the next part like a door you have to open. Would you rather stay here or step back toward the lantern?
small_talk.guidance: Choose the distance before asking about the memory. Her offer to tell you more is not a request to press.

choices.label: We can stay here. No more details needed.
choices.background: The window glows. The room behind it can stay closed.
choices.response: Thank you. The light is enough to find the path. I don't need to make it explain the room.

journal.title: The window can wait
journal.text: You stayed without making her offer into a promise to disclose more.
journal.approach: An invitation to listen is not an obligation to continue. Let her choose the next detail.

choices.label: Would a little more distance help?
choices.background: Her eyes keep finding the door.
choices.response: Yes. There. I can see both the door and you. Please keep it that way for now.

journal.title: Door and distance
journal.text: She named a place where she could see the exit and keep you in view.
journal.approach: Treat the distance she asks for as the answer, not as a starting point for negotiation.

choices.label: Let's step back toward the lantern.
choices.background: The lantern holds steady. My feet do not need to hurry.
choices.response: All right. Slowly, and where I can still see the window. I want to choose when it leaves our sight.

journal.title: The window in sight
journal.text: She agreed to move, then chose what she wanted to keep visible.
journal.approach: A practical offer can help when it leaves the pace and direction with her.

choices.label: What exactly did he do there?
choices.background: She offered a little. I reached for all of it.
choices.response: I said I could tell you more. I didn't say you could choose the part for me.

journal.title: The window closes
journal.text: She had offered a choice about listening. The question took that choice away.
journal.approach: Notice the boundary, acknowledge the pressure, and return control to her.

small_talk.prompt: The axe is his. The rest is still fog. What would help you feel safe now?
small_talk.guidance: Name present choices. Do not demand a full account or promise a confrontation.

choices.label: We can stay by the light.
choices.background: The flame makes a small circle. For a moment, that is the whole world.
choices.background_after_pressure: The circle is small. She has already had to ask me to respect its edge.
choices.response: Yes. Here, where I can see the path. The fire asks nothing of me.
choices.response_if_still_strained: Yes. Here, where I can see the path. Keep the fire between us for now; I will tell you if that changes.

journal.title: Where the light reaches
journal.text: She chose a place where the path stays visible.
journal.approach: Offer practical safety and let her choose the place.

choices.label: We don't have to look for him.
choices.background: The axe can wait. She is here.
choices.background_after_pressure: I can choose not to pursue the answer. That does not mean she owes me the rest.
choices.response: Thank you. A warning is not a summons. Let the axe be a warning enough.
choices.response_if_still_strained: Thank you. A warning is enough for tonight. I need to know you won't turn it into a reason to come closer.

journal.title: A warning, not a summons
journal.text: You heard the danger without turning the dream into a hunt.
journal.approach: Believe the warning; do not make her lead a search or confrontation.

choices.label: Tell me what you want me to know.
choices.background: I want a story. She may have something else to say.
choices.background_after_pressure: Even a gentle question can sound like the next demand when I have already asked too much.
choices.response: Only this: he is still out there. I do not owe the forest every detail for it to be true.
choices.response_if_still_strained: Only this: he is still out there. Please let that be enough for now. I need to choose when I say more.

journal.title: Enough to believe
journal.text: She named what mattered and kept the rest for herself.
journal.approach: Believe what she tells you without asking for proof.

choices.label: I'll make sure he never gets near you again.
choices.background: A promise sounds cleaner than admitting I can't control what happens after we wake.
choices.background_after_pressure: I want to end the danger for her. That want does not tell me what she asked for.
choices.processing_thought: That was a promise. I don't know if she asked me to make one.
choices.processing_thought_if_still_strained: A vow arrived where a question should have. She may remember its shape, not its promise.
choices.response: Please don't make a promise that turns this into your story. I asked you not to take the path alone; I didn't ask you to go for me.
choices.response_if_still_strained: Don't promise that. You have already made it hard to tell you what I need. I asked you not to take the path alone.

journal.title: The promise to rescue
journal.text: You answered the danger with a promise to act. Mathilda had asked you to believe the warning, not to take the choice or its consequences from her.
journal.approach: A promise to protect can still take a choice away. Ask what she wants now.

journal_if_still_strained.title: The promise to rescue
journal_if_still_strained.text: You promised to end the danger for her. Mathilda heard another decision being made without her, after she had already asked for room to choose.
journal_if_still_strained.approach: A promise to protect can still take a choice away. Ask what she wants now.

repair.prompt: She looks beyond you, as if the question has put another wall in the clearing. What now?
repair.guidance: There is still a next sentence. It does not have to be another question.

choices.label: I asked too much. We can stop.
choices.background: I hear my question again. It sounded different in my head.
choices.processing_thought: An apology is not a lever. I can't make it open the next sentence.
choices.processing_thought_if_still_strained: She heard the apology. I still need to keep the distance I promised.
choices.response: Thank you. Stay there a moment. I can find the path again.
choices.background_after_pressure: I can say the right thing now. She may still need time to believe it.
choices.response_if_still_strained: Thank you for stopping. Stay there a moment. I can find the path again, but I need the distance to remain real.

journal.title: Room to return
journal.text: You named the pressure and gave her space to choose whether to continue.
journal.approach: A repair starts with recognizing the impact, then leaving the next move to her.

journal_if_still_strained.title: Room to return
journal_if_still_strained.text: You stopped pressing. She let you stay, but asked for the distance to remain real. The apology changed what happened next; it did not undo what came before.
journal_if_still_strained.approach: Let a repair take time. Keep the boundary you have just acknowledged.

choices.label: Help me understand what happened.
choices.background: There has to be a question that makes the fragments line up.
choices.background_after_pressure: I am calling this understanding. It still asks her to make the fragments fit for me.
choices.processing_thought: I called it a request. I can hear what it asked her to do.
choices.processing_thought_if_still_strained: I asked her to do the work of making this easier for me.
choices.response: I don't know how to make them line up for you. I have only said what I could.
choices.response_if_still_strained: I already said what I could. Asking me to make sense of it for you is still another way of asking for more.

journal.title: Make it make sense
journal.text: You framed your need as a request for understanding. It still made her responsible for resolving your uncertainty.
journal.approach: A gentle question can still ask someone to do more work. Leave room for an unfinished answer.

journal_if_still_strained.title: Make it make sense
journal_if_still_strained.text: After she had already asked for room, you asked her to arrange the fragments into a story for you. The pressure deepened, even though the question sounded gentle.
journal_if_still_strained.approach: A gentle question can still ask someone to do more work. Leave room for an unfinished answer.

choices.label: I believe you. I won't make you prove it.
choices.background: No proof. Just her face, and what she has been carrying.
choices.processing_thought: Belief doesn't return what my last question spent.
choices.response: Then let me say only what I can. The light is still there.
choices.background_after_pressure: Belief is not a clean slate. It is one thing I can offer without asking her to carry me.
choices.response_if_still_strained: I hear you. I still need the light between us. I can say only what I can, and leave the rest for another time.

journal.title: Belief without proof
journal.text: You offered trust without asking her to earn it with details.
journal.approach: Believing her leaves the next choice with her.

journal_if_still_strained.title: Belief without proof
journal_if_still_strained.text: You offered trust. Mathilda accepted the words but kept the light between you. Belief arrived before closeness did.
journal_if_still_strained.approach: Let trust be an offer, not a claim that the other person should feel safe now.

question: What do you wish someone understood?
question_guidance: Choose what is yours to say. You may keep the rest private. If she turns away, step back; a name is not the same as a warning.

branches.label: I said no.
branches.background: The word is small. It is still enough.
branches.processing_thought: The word is finished. No one gets to ask it into a longer shape.
branches.response: You said it. I heard you. The word can stay here without becoming a whole story.

journal.title: A word left whole
journal.text: You chose to name the boundary. Mathilda did not ask you to defend it.
journal.approach: A no needs no supporting evidence or explanation.

branches.ophelia: At the first bend, she remembers that no is a complete sentence.
branches.mathilda: By the cups, she remembers she does not owe anyone an explanation.

branches.label: I went still. That wasn't yes.
branches.background: I know that stillness. It does not mean yes.
branches.processing_thought: Stillness didn't answer him. It doesn't have to answer me either.
branches.response: You went still. I believe you. You don't have to prove what your body did to survive.

journal.title: Still is not yes
journal.text: You chose to name what stillness did not mean.
journal.approach: Do not mistake freezing or silence for agreement.

branches.ophelia: She leaves the lamp where it is and does not ask why the door stayed shut.
branches.mathilda: She sits by the fire until her hands remember they are her own.

branches.label: I was trying to get away.
branches.background: The way back felt farther than it was.
branches.processing_thought: There is a way out in the memory. The road is not the same as a decision.
branches.response: You were trying to get away. The way back can belong to you now.

journal.title: A way back
journal.text: You chose the part of the story that points toward freedom now.
journal.approach: Offer choices about what happens next; do not take over.

branches.ophelia: The house is not a debt. She can leave it and return by choice.
branches.mathilda: The path past the tent is hers to take, or not take.

branches.label: I can't say it yet.
branches.background: Not yet. The silence after it does not feel empty.
branches.processing_thought: A silence can be chosen. It doesn't need me to finish it.
branches.response: Then we can leave it there. I can sit with you without asking again.

journal.title: Not yet shared
journal.text: You chose to keep the sentence private. The conversation made room for that.
journal.approach: Respect an unfinished answer. Do not ask again in another form.

branches.ophelia: At the first bend, the unsaid sentence can stay unsaid.
branches.mathilda: By the spare cup, there is room for a pause.

branches.label: I can stay beside you without an answer.
branches.background: Quiet with her. It does not have to speak for us.
branches.processing_thought: Company can keep its distance. The snow has room for both of us.
branches.response: Then stay where I can see you. We can let the path be a path for a while.

journal.title: Company without demand
journal.text: You chose to remain present without turning the silence into a question.
journal.approach: Offer company, then let the other person decide whether to speak.

branches.ophelia: At the first bend, they walk together without making the silence carry a message.
branches.mathilda: By the spare cup, Ophelia stays in sight. Nothing is asked of the quiet.

branches.label: What would help you feel safer right now?
branches.background: What does she need now, here in the snow, with this light?
branches.processing_thought: The fire keeps no record of why someone came to it.
branches.response: Keep the light between us and the trees. We can leave when I say. That is enough for now.

journal.title: Safety in the present
journal.text: You asked about the moment in front of her, not for a complete account of the past.
journal.approach: Ask about present needs. Let her set the next step and the distance.

branches.ophelia: She leaves the lamp where it is and asks what would help now.
branches.mathilda: The fire stays in view. For this moment, the path is hers to choose.

ending: I'm sorry I'm still being so vague. The one who cut the trees is still out there. I saw his axe by the path. Please don't take the path alone.

unresolved.response: I'm sorry. I gave you fragments and still couldn't say what they meant. The warning has no name yet.
unresolved.response_after_passing_lantern: I remember the lantern from the path. I kept walking, and now I can't tell what the light was trying to keep alive. Maybe I was waiting for someone to stop with me.
unresolved.ophelia: The trail offered three moments. She passed the warm window without finding another clue. Morning brings her home with no answer.
unresolved.ophelia_after_passing_lantern: The three images followed her home. The lantern did not; she remembers it only as a light behind her on the path.
unresolved.mathilda: She woke with a cold feeling and no picture she could hold. By morning, even the warning had lost its words.
unresolved.mathilda_after_passing_lantern: She remembers the lantern burning behind them. In the morning, she cannot say what she hoped Ophelia would notice there.

journal.title: A warning without its words
journal.text: The warm window held the clearest memory. It stayed unopened, and the fragments never became an answer.
journal.approach: Follow the trail and let the warm-window clue settle beside one other moment. A fragment is not a failure.

journal_after_passing_lantern.title: The lantern left to weather
journal_after_passing_lantern.text: You saw the flame from the path and kept walking. The sisters, thread and window stayed with you, but the exposed lantern remained outside the reading. Mathilda's warning returned as a fragment.
journal_after_passing_lantern.approach: Before the final answer, shelter the flame or leave it and come back. A second look is enough; you do not have to make the light safe.

strained.response: I can tell you enough from here. He is still out there. I saw his axe by the path. Please don't take it alone. The rest will have to wait.
strained.ophelia: The warning reached her across the snow. In the morning, she remembers the axe clearly and the distance more clearly still.
strained.mathilda: She remembered the warning, but not how the conversation ended. The lantern was still between them when she woke.

journal.title: The warning at a distance
journal.text: The warning reached you. The closeness did not return in time. The journal keeps both the words and their cost.
journal.approach: Believe the warning without asking for the rest. Leave room for trust to take longer than an apology.

ruptured.response: I wanted to tell you. Then it became something you needed from me. I can't stay in this room now.
ruptured.ophelia: She tried to make the answer arrive. In the morning, the door is shut, and the question is all she remembers.
ruptured.mathilda: She woke at the edge of the light. The path behind her had closed before she could name what she feared.

journal.title: The conversation closed
journal.text: Pushing for certainty turned the warning into a demand. The dream ended without the words Mathilda had been trying to find.
journal.approach: A bad turn is not permanent. Slow down, acknowledge the pressure, and let her set the pace.
